result:
**Short version:** The three rewritten passages are below. Seven wording changes depend on my reading of the original, so check them before you paste. I added no term definitions.

## Passage 1

```
- Block save. A run is up to 16 consecutive tokens inside one 16-token block.
  - Transpose: the K rows of the run are transposed in registers.
  - Write: the result is written as whole 64-byte lines. Each line takes one store.
  - Mask: a store is masked when the run does not fill the block.
  - Run of one token: this run still uses the scatter. Every decode step produces a run of one token.
- Sharing.
  - Claiming: the main thread and the idle main helper threads claim the blocks from one counter.
  - Helper count: the generated plugin decides the count for each pass. The count is not fixed. The traced runs used 7 helpers at tp2.
  - Calling thread: single-worker callers and passes of at most 16 tokens store on the calling thread. The single-worker callers are the handwritten plugins and the unit tests.
```

## Passage 2

```
Where write keeps less than read. This happens in two kinds of rows:

- two writers in one DSU at 160 KiB
- eight writers at any size

In these rows the writers share one path. The 32 GB/s write streams saturate that path sooner than the 9 to 12 GB/s read streams do. The path is one of these:

- one DSU's mesh port
- the DRAM write limit (section 8)
```

## Passage 3

```
Codex gave a final assessment. The plan now states it.

The rows can show four things:

- whether the gain needs the prefetchers
- whether the prefetchers target the L3
- whether demand reads find lines in the L3
- whether more requests wait at the home nodes

The rows alone cannot separate two hypotheses:

- Your hypothesis: data waits in the L3 before the core asks for it.
- The alternative: the DSU handles the same prefetch requests faster.

The external-fetch count with the L3 on stays "Insufficient data". It stays that way until a counter's source and population are established on the target.

The bit-6 boot is the only proposed intervention that acts directly on the mechanism in your hypothesis.
```

## Readings to check

| Passage | Original | Rewrite |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | "keeps the scatter" | "still uses the scatter" |
| 2 | "write loses" | "write keeps less than read" |
| 2 | "DRAM write ceiling" | "DRAM write limit" |
| 3 | "your picture" | "your hypothesis" |
| 3 | "ahead of the core" | "before the core asks for it" |
| 3 | "on the table" | "proposed" |
| 3 | "acts on your picture" | "acts on the mechanism in your hypothesis" |

Change "limit" back to "ceiling" if section 8 uses "ceiling" as its name.

## Terms not defined

I do not have the project's meaning for these terms. Each one needs a definition at first use, unless the full document already gives one:

- Passage 1: K rows, scatter, generated plugin, tp2
- Passage 2: DSU, mesh port, "keeps"
- Passage 3: Codex, L3, home nodes, external-fetch count, bit-6 boot
